In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a direct effect of LPS on hepatic catalase, nor that the presence of a hepatoma affects the enzyme activity in mice.
the effect of tumour induction on the response of catalase activity to LPS is dependent on the genetic make-up of the mice and the dose of LPS.
there is an influence of LPS on hepatic catalase, which is strain-dependent and which is also influenced by the presence of tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of LPS on hepatic catalase in normal and tumour-bearing mice seems to be influenced by both LPS responsiveness and the presence of a malignant tumour.
the LPS responsiveness is not the same as the tumour susceptibility of the host.
LPS responsiveness is a genetic characteristic of the mouse and that this characteristic can be modified by tumour induction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of endotoxins on the catalase activity in liver is not only strain dependent but also depends on the dose of the endotoxin used.
there is no evidence that tumour-bearing mice are more sensitive to the effects of endotoxin.
